_note: THE ONE PLACE A PRICE IS WRITTEN DOWN. tools/cost.py reads this and nothing else;
BOM.md's prose prices are for a human to read, and drifted from each other (three
different per-motor supply currents, two different junction gaps). A price here has
a source and a date, or it is marked unverified and the total says so.
verified: 'v' = read off the supplier's own product page. 'm' = from a listing,
search result or memory, NOT the product page -- cost.py counts these separately
and prints the total twice, with and without them, because the user's rule is that
a price comes off the product page.
qty: the price break this figure came from. cost.py does NOT interpolate breaks --
if the instrument needs 40 and the price is @10, it uses the @10 figure and says so.

petg-gf.source: Tinmorry 10-roll pack, blended over the order basket
petg-gf.what: WAS $29.99/kg from a list price. The store sells a TEN-ROLL PACK -- 10 Rolls Glass Fiber PETG Filament, 1 KG 1 Spool, Frosted Black/White/Grey -- at $175.00, in stock, i.e. $17.50/kg. A ten-instrument order needs 41.0 kg, so the real basket is 4 packs + 1 single spool at $25.99 = $725.99, which blends to $17.71/kg. That is the number here. Measured at a real Tinmorry checkout 2026-09-30 (cart built, shipping quoted, cart cleared, nothing ordered): SHIPPING FREE on 57.35 kg gross, ships from the USA in 7-14 days, and NO SALES TAX LINE AT ALL -- total equalled subtotal. So this is already landed. One caveat: a SINGLE instrument cannot reach this rate (4.1 kg off singles is $31.70/kg); the ten-instrument basis is what buys it.

boards.assembly_note: setup and feeder are PER ORDER (so per ten instruments); joints are per board

_note: MEASURED on jlcpcb.com's instant quote, 2026-09-30, at the form's DEFAULTS:
FR-4, 1.6 mm, green, HASL(with lead), 1 oz outer, tented vias, single PCB,
Industrial/Consumer. Price is for the WHOLE quantity, not per board.
These replace a formula that was wrong by 2x to 12x. The old model charged a
$2.00 MINIMUM PER BOARD, so 100 small tee boards came to $200 against a real
$16.60 -- JLCPCB prices a batch, not a board, and the minimum is per ORDER.
The error was worst exactly where the instrument has most boards.
⚠ Re-measure before ordering. Quotes move, and these are one day's numbers.
Fitted to the rows above. base + area_rate x cm2, then extra boards beyond
the quoted 10 at per_extra_board. The 2-layer split at 100 mm is real and
visible in the data: 72x34 (both sides under 100) quotes $5.00 while the
LARGER-in-one-dimension 139x20 quotes $6.90 on LESS area.

_assembly_note: MEASURED 2026-09-30 on a real JLCPCB PCBA quote: can_tee's own gerber + BOM + CPL
uploaded, Economic PCBA, qty 50, 3 parts (2 THT connectors, 1 0603 resistor).
PCB Price                 $11.30   engineering 8.00 + film 0.30 + board 3.00
Economic PCBA Price       $35.98
Setup Fee                $8.24   per board DESIGN per order
Stencil                  $1.55   per board DESIGN per order
Components (3 items)    $10.79   50 boards' worth of parts
SMT Assembly             $0.17   100 joints  -> $0.0017 each
Hand-soldering           $3.61   600 THT pins -> $0.0060 each
Manual Assembly          $9.97   100 THT parts -> $0.0997 each
Nitrogen reflow          $1.65   an option, not modelled -- turn it off
Total                     $47.28
WHAT THIS OVERTURNED. The $0.0017 per SMT joint was right. Everything else was
not. Hand-soldering is $0.006 a pin, not the $0.20 guessed here yesterday -- 33x
out -- but THT also carries a SEPARATE $0.0997 per PART placed, which nothing in
the model knew about. Net for can_tee: $0.27 a board against $2.40 guessed.
Setup is $8.24 and it is PER DESIGN, not $25.00 once for the order, so ten board
designs pay it ten times.
ONE DATA POINT, Economic, qty 50. Standard PCBA prices differently -- it shows a
'Feeders Loading fee' where Economic shows 'Setup Fee' -- and JLCPCB forces
Standard above a qty threshold, where a board under 70 mm a side then gets EDGE
RAILS added. Measured on can_tee at qty 100: the board charge went $6.00 -> $37.40
because the 49.5x16 outline was padded out to 71.5x70. See boards.rails_note.
rails_note: MEASURED: can_tee qty 100 was pushed to Standard PCBA, which requires every side
over 70 mm and adds edge rails. 49.5 x 16 became 71.5 x 70 and the board line went
from $6.00 to $37.40. At qty 50 the same board stays Economic, needs no rails, and
the board line is $3.00. This is a REAL cost cliff that depends on order quantity,
and it lands on our two smallest, most numerous boards: can_tee (10 per instrument)
and lever_sensor (11 per instrument, 31 x 21.9 mm). Panelising is the escape --
JLCPCB itself offered a 5 x 15 panel -- and nothing in this model represents it.
_stock_note: SOURCING RISK found while quoting can_tee: C157914 (S8B-XH-A, the 8-way CAN
connector) had 65 pieces in JLCPCB's library on 2026-09-30, against the 100 a
ten-instrument order needs. The quote would not proceed until the quantity came
down under stock. It is a stocked JST part, so this is a JLCPCB-library depth
problem rather than a dead part -- but assembly is only turnkey while they hold it.

DECIDED 2026-09-30 by the user after the survey: the 2GB SKU caps at ONE unit per order across the trade (PiShop max 1; CanaKit max 1 per customer with multiple orders AUTO-CANCELLED; Adafruit and SparkFun cap-free but out of stock), so it cannot be bought ten at a time at all. The 1GB caps at TEN, which is exactly the order. That is -$20/instrument against the old 2GB line. THE RISK IS RAM, not price: Dexed + USB gadget + USB host has to fit 1GB headless. If it does not, the fallback is the 4GB at $100 (no cap), +$45/instrument.

_note: SHIPPING, SALES TAX AND TARIFF, measured at real checkouts on 2026-09-30 with the
user's own address (Berkeley CA 94702) and a TEN-INSTRUMENT order in the cart.
Nothing was purchased.
THE ONE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES THE TARIFF QUESTION is whether a vendor ships
DDP -- Delivered Duty Paid. JLCPCB's DHL line says DDP outright, so its quoted
shipping ALREADY CONTAINS the duty and there is nothing further to add. Makerbase
ships the motors from Liwan District on 'free shipping' and collects no US tax and
no duty at checkout, so that one is NOT landed cost: whatever duty applies arrives
later, from the carrier. That is an exposure this file can name but cannot price,
because the rate is policy and changes.
SALES TAX IS NOT ONE NUMBER. Lace's checkout computed 8.00% on $1,470; PiShop's
computed 10.25% on $350, which IS the Berkeley headline rate. Same address, same
state, 2.25 points apart -- so tax is a per-vendor measurement like shipping, and
a single assumed rate across the BOM would be wrong in both directions.
counted_in_unit_price says whether the money is ALREADY inside the unit price
elsewhere in this file. The Jameco tariff is (mechanical.psu_24v_150w carries its
$3.59 share), so cost.py must not add it twice.

makerbase_motors.what: 100 x SERVO42D CAN MT (10 per instrument) = $3,399.00 -- free shipping (10-16 d); paid options 4PX $8.99, DHL/UPS $22.80, standard $3.99. NO tax and NO duty collected at checkout, so this is NOT landed cost. tariff_unpriced_upper_usd is a BOUND, not a measurement: 21.0% -- the one rate anybody has actually seen itemised, on Jameco's power supplies -- applied to the motor order, giving $713.79 an order or $71.38 an instrument. THE RATE IS BORROWED FROM THE WRONG COMMODITY CODE (8504.40 is power supplies; a driver-plus-motor is 8501.10 territory) and duty rates are policy, so treat it as an order of magnitude and the worst case, not a forecast. SEARCHED FOR A US-STOCKED ALTERNATIVE AND THERE IS NONE: the Amazon listings for this part are dropships -- 'SERVO42D CAN MB' at $53.71 is the DRIVER ALONE, no motor, ships in 6-7 days with delivery quoted three to four weeks out, i.e. from China anyway. So there is no way to buy this part with the duty already paid, and Makerbase direct stays the cheapest route even at the full borrowed rate ($41.13 landed worst case vs $53.71 for less hardware).
